input.quote: 14. TERMINATION. Subject to Section 4 hereof, TrueLink will continue to provide the requested Hosting Services and Support Services until the last day of the month following the month in which Client provides TrueLink with a written notice of its election to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty or stipulated sum on us (Client), so the preferred position is met and no redline is warranted. I checked each place such an amount would sit: the termination and term provisions (§§ 13-14, p0078-p0079) let either party exit on notice with services simply running to the last day of the following month and no exit charge, early-termination fee or accelerated/minimum payment on termination; the compensation provisions (§ 5 and § 6, p0045/p0047) contain only fees for services actually requested and a monthly fee floor for services delivered during the term, plus a contested-amounts mechanic, with no late-payment penalty or interest charge; the anti-spamming covenant (§ 7, p0049) and § 8(f) (p0058) give TrueLink only technical and general legal/equitable enforcement rights, not a per-message or fixed penalty; and § 8 contains no stipulated damages for breach of Client covenants. Client's indemnity in § 12(a) (p0071-p0072) and the cumulative-remedies clause (§ 21, p0087) are actual-loss/at-law remedies, not pre-agreed liquidated sums, and the only liability cap (p0077) runs in our favour against TrueLink. No fallback analysis is needed because no Customer-payable liquidated amount exists at all; we would resist introducing one, and any unavoidable early-termination fee should be capped at three months' fees.

mappings.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
